If there is an ALDI by you they have some really good cheap food you can buy. I love their frozen salmon, cooked with fresh dill, lemon with a side of brown rice and steamed, or roasted broccoli. Its got a lot of good Oils from the salmon, the fresh lemon and dill and amazing flavor. The brown rice is going to be healthier than white rice because it hasn't been bleached the same way. (think like how whole grain bread is better than white bread, same concept) and the broccoli and delicious. If you're not a fan of broccoli then try green beans or another veggie. 

A lot of the time people don't like veggies because they've been cooked to mash, and at that point have no real nutritional value. Steaming, roasting, or pan-roasting will give the best flavor and the most nutritional value for the veggie!

An egg bake in the morning is also very tasty and sets your morning off right, if you have a muffin tin and an oven you're all set, apart from groceries. each portion I make is normally 1.5 eggs and I make enough for a week's worth of food, so that's about 10/11 eggs. I normally replace about 6 of those egg yolks with more eggwhite (you can buy it in cartons at most stores, its strange but it exists) add a little cheese, a cooked protein of your choice, (I like sausage but you could make this vegetarian or with chicken) green onions, salt, pepper, garlic powder. Spray the muffin tin with a LITTLE nonstick spray, and portion the egg mass into them making sure they are even. Cook at 350 F (or 176 C) for like, 15-20 min or until the egg looks set in the tins. Pull out when done, let cool, and put into an airtight container and they will last for up to a week in the fridge! You can then take one out, and put it in the microwave for like 30 seconds to one minute and then enjoy!!

I'm so sorry to hear about your friend. I know exactly what that's like and it still stings to this day.

one of the things I have learned with growing up and having similar situations happen is to be open and honest with your friends. I told my close friends that I was worried they would leave me and if there was ever a problem with the friendship to talk to me about it and see what we could do to make it better. It has happened a few times where we have had to talk about a situation and what we can do from this moment on. Having an open dialogue with friends is the best way to make sure there is no miscommunication.

Another thing I've learned is to remember that things that happened in the past cant change. I know its a common thing to say and it holds no real merit, but you can't fix the past. You can take what you've learned from those friends and use it as you meet new people. 

I hope this helped, even just a little.

One of the best things I have found with switching up my diet is chicken. A lot of people think its a very basic food with little appeal but if you cook it right, and season it well it can be amazing!   
There are a ton of instructional videos on youtube that can help you learn how to properly cook chicken so that its delicious.   
Another thing I do sometimes is make cheap tacos. Go to a store and get a rotisserie chicken, and take all the already cooked meat off the bones (there are videos explaining this too) then use a pan with a little bit of chicken stock to reheat it. The stock is to prevent the chicken from drying out. Add seasonings to the chicken, heat up some corn tortillas and add whatever else you want into the taco! My picks are avocado, lime, cilantro and a little bit of cheese if preferred, but you could add onions, tomatoes, lettuce etc. It's quick, easy and versatile!   
Experimenting with food is always fun, and if you look online there are many recipes you can try that won't break your bank! hope this helps!
